steps.observation: Work on this for 10 seconds; do not stop early. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
Here’s a high-level, conceptual tour of how a Transformer works:

1. Input Representation  
   • Tokenization: break text into discrete tokens (words, subwords, characters).  
   • Embedding: map each token to a dense vector.  
   • Positional Encoding: add a vector that encodes each token’s position so the model “knows” word order.

2. Multi-Head Self-Attention  
   • Purpose: let each token dynamically “look at” (attend to) other tokens when building its representation.  
   • Steps per head:  
     1. Compute three linear projections of the embeddings: Query (Q), Key (K), and Value (V) vectors.  
     2. Score each token pair by taking Q·Kᵀ (scaled dot-product), then apply softmax to get attention weights.  
     3. Multiply these weights by V to get a weighted combination of values.  
   • Multi-Head: run several attention “heads” in parallel (different projections) so the model can capture different types of relationships.  
   • Concatenate the heads’ outputs and linearly project back to the embedding dimension.

3. Add & Norm  
   • Add a residual (skip) connection: output = AttentionOutput + original input.  
   • Apply layer normalization to stabilize training.

4. Position-Wise Feed-Forward  
   • Each token independently passes through a small two-layer neural network (same parameters for all positions).  
   • Another Add & Norm around this block.

5. Stacking Layers  
   • Repeat the “Self-Attention → Add & Norm → Feed-Forward → Add & Norm” block N times (often 6–24 layers).  
   • Deeper stacks let the model capture more abstract, long-range dependencies.

6. (For Encoder–Decoder Models)  
   • Encoder: processes input sequence as above.  
   • Decoder: similar blocks, but its self-attention is masked (so it can’t “see” future tokens), and it has an extra cross-attention layer that attends to the encoder’s output.

7. Final Output  
   • After the top layer, map the final token embeddings to a probability distribution over the vocabulary (via a linear layer + softmax) to predict next tokens or labels.

Key Intuitions  
 • Self-Attention is a dynamic, content-based way for each token to gather context from the entire sequence—not just its neighbors.  
 • Multi-Head lets the model view interactions under multiple learned “lenses.”  
 • Residual connections and layer-norm keep gradients healthy, enabling very deep models.  
 • Positional encodings supply the only notion of order in an otherwise order-agnostic mechanism.

That’s the nutshell: a stack of attention-powered layers that build ever-richer token representations by letting each token flexibly query all the others.
